messages:
alex: quick sanity check — ran the warmup smoke suite against the new bucketed-seqlen heuristic on staging, results below.

alex: TL;DR: p95 token latency down ~18% for seq_len >=512, but small seq_len (<=64) saw a small p50 regression (~4%). suspect warmup ordering + batchshape selection.

priya: can you paste the command you used so i can reproduce? 

alex: sure — used the smoke script: 

alex: ```
./tools/warmup-smoke --profile=autotune-v2 --model=gpt-small --buckets="[32,64,128,256,512,1024]" --waves=3 --parallel=8
```

samir: nice. did you toggle per-model vs global kernel prefs? last time global prefs hurt small models.

alex: ran both. global kernel-prefer=fp16-kernel was default. then per-model override to fast-attn for mid seqlens. observed that per-model overrides cut the small-seq regression, but increases mem pressure slightly.

emily: any cache hit differences? i remember prefix/KV caching can interact badly with bucketed warmup if you prefill wrong shapes.

alex: good call — cache hit-rate for 512+ increased as expected. but 32/64 had lower cache usage because warmup prefills were grouped into 128 batches, so the tiny sequences didn't get KV prefill before steady state.

priya: maybe we need a staged "waterfall" warmup: first wave targeted at the lowest seq-len bucket to prime KV cache, then larger waves. that would keep batching efficiency while avoiding cold tiny requests.

samir: i like waterfall. we should also limit the per-wave batchshape diversity so prefill shapes match the bucket. e.g. wave1: bucket 32 -> batchshape (32 x N small), wave2: 128 etc.

alex: agreed. quick sketch of policy: 

alex: ```
warmup_policy: 
  waves: 4
  order: [smallest_to_largest] # waterfall
  per_wave_target: {min_qps: 10, duration_s: 20}
  batchshape_hint: true # prefer batch shapes aligned to bucket
```

emily: also add TTL-based eviction for KV entries from warmup-only prefills so they don't crowd real traffic caches. TTL ~60s?

samir: TTL makes sense. Maybe make TTL adaptive: shorter for lower-util models. fallback eviction policy LRU after TTL expiry.

priya: rollout plan? can we A/B the new waterfall warmup as a canary for 5% traffic on dedicated pools first?

alex: yes — will make the rollout flag `runtime.warmup.waterfall=v1` and schedule a canary: 5% dedicated -> 20% -> full. will collect p50/p95/alloc-failures + mem tail.

ci-bot: deploy plan created: warmup/waterfall - canary 5% (dedicated) by alex; changelist CL: 61234.

alex: follow-ups: 1) implement per-bucket batchshape hinting, 2) waterfall ordering + adaptive TTLs, 3) add smoke tests for tiny-seq steady-state regression. i'll open RFC follow-up with benchmarks.

priya: thanks — once RFC is up i'll review. small ask: add a smoke that simulates frontend traffic mix (70% small, 20% mid, 10% long) so we don't overfit to single-bucket gains.

alex: will do. tagging @priya for review and @samir for cache eviction logic. :thumbsup:

emily: fyi i annotated a couple of logs where kv-prefill shows up as "warmup:prefill" so we can filter in dashboards.

samir: cool — i can add a heatmap for prefill vs real-kv hits.

alex: awesome. closing for now, will post RFC link once it's up.
